ai.title: Freebuff CLI 0.0.200 release
ai.summary: Freebuff CLI version 0.0.200 is published, bundling several functional changes since 0.0.199. On local Linux terminals, a successful OSC 52 clipboard copy that cannot be verified appends LINUX_OSC52_ONLY_HINT to the toast and extends its display duration to 6000 ms to warn that paste may be empty without wl-clipboard or xclip. eli5.text: Freebuff CLI 0.0.200 adds stricter safety guards for advertiser-funded tasks and improves how the terminal handles copying on Linux. For sponsored runs, the system now blocks commands that could enter your Windows subsystem, wipe databases, or start and stop containers, ensuring these automated tasks cannot interfere with your personal work or running services. If a sponsored task needs an account credential, the system asks you for it in a hidden field and automatically hides that secret from the AI's view in all output and error messages. In addition, the CLI now shows a helpful hint when you copy text on a Linux terminal without standard clipboard tools installed, telling you exactly which software to add to make pasting work. The release also tightens privacy wording to clarify that advertising partners can only evaluate connected cloud repositories and cannot train on your code.

The session hook `use-freebuff-session.ts` now probes for a legacy single-session hour left by a dead pre-multi-session CLI process via `deadLegacyFreebuffOwner`, resuming it without a new purchase on update restarts. The placement model in `freebuff-placements.ts` adds the `partner` format and two new slots (`Desktop-Partner-Skill-Picker`, `Desktop-Partner-Composer-PR`) that are exclusive to a single advertiser and excluded from self-serve targeting.
ai.evidence: The diff in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` bumps the `version` from `0.0.200` to `0.0.201`. The release notes cite member commits `a78f5290` and `9e3fdf76`, whose source hunks show `deadLegacyFreebuffOwner` in `cli/src/utils/freebuff-instance-owner.ts` and `partner` slots in `common/src/constants/freebuff-placements.ts`.

eli5.text: The CLI now preserves the remaining time from a previous session when you update the app, so you do not lose the time you already paid for. It also adds new ad slots that display an advertiser's own branding directly next to the skill picker or composer instead of showing a generic ad card. These new slots are exclusive to specific ad deals and cannot be targeted by regular advertisers in the console. If your previous session has ended or belongs to a different account, the new version safely falls back to starting a fresh session rather than trying to reuse the old one.

entries.title: Agent Runtime update: model-compaction
entries.summary: Agent Runtime, SDK changes across 2 file(s) (+308/−13).

ai.title: Binary payloads elided from compaction and rewind counts from the end
ai.summary: The agent runtime now names media and long base64 payloads instead of serializing their bytes into the compaction request, so a screenshot-heavy thread compacts in one pass instead of restarting across many large summarizer calls. The SDK's truncateRunStateAtUserTurn gains an optional totalUserTurns parameter that, when supplied, places the rewind boundary from the end of messageHistory rather than counting user turns from the start, which previously miscounted Stop notes and compaction summaries as user turns. Two other behavior surfaces in this commit are the parseCompactionSummary double-decoding fix and the mechanical fallback logging path.
ai.evidence: packages/agent-runtime/src/model-compaction.ts adds elideBinaryStrings and omittedBinary to replace base64 media parts with placeholder strings during compaction, and the diff hunk shows the media part branch returning omittedBinary(part.mediaType). sdk/src/compact-run-state.ts adds the optional totalUserTurns parameter to truncateRunStateAtUserTurn and rewrites the cut logic to count from the end of messageHistory when it is supplied.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the rollout path for totalUserTurns to the hosts that would pass it.

changes.what: Media parts and long base64 strings are now named with placeholders instead of serialized into compaction requests.
truncateRunStateAtUserTurn gains a totalUserTurns parameter that places the rewind boundary from the end of messageHistory when provided.

eli5.text: The AI assistant no longer wastes time re-summarizing entire chat histories when those histories contain large screenshots or image files. Previously, every screenshot a tool returned (like a picture of code or a webpage) was crammed into the text the assistant tried to summarize, turning one quick summary into dozens of slow rounds. Now those images are skipped and named instead, so a session full of screenshots compacts in a single step. This speeds up and stabilizes the assistant's memory-trimming for anyone editing earlier parts of a long conversation, since the part that picks where to rewind now counts from the end of the chat instead of getting confused by internal notes and saved summaries.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI 0.0.203 elides binary payloads in compaction
ai.summary: Release 0.0.203 introduces binary payload elision in the agent runtime to prevent base64 data from inflating context token counts during compaction. The new function elideBinaryStrings in packages/agent-runtime/src/model-compaction.ts replaces media parts and long base64 runs with a placeholder string when serializing history for the summarizer. This prevents screenshot-heavy threads from triggering massive sequential summarizer calls that previously stalled the agent loop.
ai.evidence: The primary diff shows a version bump in freebuff/cli/release/package.json from 0.0.202 to 0.0.203. The release member source evidence cites changes in packages/agent-runtime/src/model-compaction.ts where a new elideBinaryStrings function is added to replace base64 data URLs with placeholders during history serialization.

eli5.text: This release fixes a problem where saving large images or files in your coding history caused the AI assistant to stop responding. Previously, huge data strings from screenshots or embedded files were copied into the summary process, which could consume millions of units of processing space and cause long waits or complete failures. Now, the assistant labels these large data blocks instead of copying them, ensuring the summary process stays manageable and threads do not freeze. Additionally, the assistant now correctly remembers your conversation when you edit or undo previous steps. Previously, if you stopped and restarted a task multiple times, editing an earlier message could cause the assistant to forget most of the conversation because it miscounted what constituted a new user turn. The fix ensures that only your actual prompts are counted for memory, so your context remains intact even in long or frequently paused sessions.

entries.title: CLI update: chat
entries.summary: New files: `cli/src/utils/fatal-crash-report.ts`.

ai.title: CLI ships previous-launcher fatal crash telemetry on next launch
ai.summary: A new fatal-crash-report module writes a bounded crash report (error name, first 300 chars of message, first 20 stack frames, version/platform/uptime, and whether a Freebuff hour was held) synchronously to last-fatal-crash.json as the process exits, and the next launch reads and ships it as a cli.fatal_crash analytics event before the session begins. The report is dropped if older than 7 days or corrupt, recording and reading never throw, and a report is consumed exactly once. Concurrently, useGravityAd now returns a frozen NO_RESPONSE_ADS singleton via visibleResponseAds so hidden inline ads no longer re-trigger chat's layout effect each render, and SDK event handlers are wrapped in isolateUiHandler so a throwing UI update is logged and the agent run continues instead of becoming an unhandled fatal rejection. SIGPIPE is now explicitly ignored and excluded from CLI_RENDERER_EXIT_SIGNALS so a broken-pipe write no longer tears down the renderer and risks an exit-141 death, and external exits (terminal closed, killed, launcher gone) keep an active Freebuff hour for resume via the new keepSlotForResume path instead of ending it.
ai.evidence: New module cli/src/utils/fatal-crash-report.ts defines recordFatalCrashSync and takePreviousFatalCrash; cli/src/index.tsx calls takePreviousFatalCrash at launch and fires AnalyticsEvent.CLI_FATAL_CRASH, and common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts adds CLI_FATAL_CRASH='cli.fatal_crash' to the enum; common/src/util/analytics-sampling.ts adds CLI_FATAL_CRASH to ALWAYS_TRACK_EVENTS.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show whether a server-side endpoint exists to receive the cli.fatal_crash event payload or how the heldFreebuffSession flag is consumed downstream.

changes.what: Added fatal-crash-report.ts with recordFatalCrashSync writing a bounded report to last-fatal-crash.json and takePreviousFatalCrash reading and consuming it; index.tsx ships the previous report as cli.fatal_crash on launch.

Added CLI_RENDERER_EXIT_SIGNALS (SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGQUIT, SIGABRT, SIGHUP, SIGBREAK, SIGBUS, excluding SIGPIPE) and an explicit SIGPIPE ignore handler in renderer-cleanup.ts; createCliRenderer now uses these signals so SIGPIPE no longer destroys the renderer.
External exits (terminal closed, killed, launcher gone) now call keepSlotForResume to retain an active Freebuff hour for the next launch instead of ending it.

Added visibleResponseAds and a frozen NO_RESPONSE_ADS singleton in use-gravity-ad.ts, and chat.tsx now passes visibleResponseAds(showInlineAds, responseAds) into the message-block context so hidden ads keep a stable identity.

Wrapped createStreamChunkHandler and createEventHandler in isolateUiHandler so a throwing SDK event updates are logged (bounded to MAX_UI_HANDLER_FAILURE_LOGS_PER_RUN per run) and the agent run continues instead of fatal-exiting.

eli5.text: When the assistant app crashes, it now saves a small note about the crash locally as it shuts down, and the next time you open the app it reads that note and sends a quiet crash report. This helps fix recurring crashes without asking you for screenshots, and the report is deleted after use. A broken-pipe write (like output redirected to a closed command) no longer kills the app with a confusing exit-code-141, hidden inline ads no longer cause the chat to re-render in a loop, and if the app is closed by an outside signal while a free session is running, that free time is kept for the next launch instead of being ended early. The crash report only ever ships once and is ignored if it is older than a week or unreadable, so it never blocks a normal startup.

ai.title: Move CLI claim prefix to shared constants for version 0.0.204
ai.summary: Release 0.0.204 centralizes the Freebuff CLI purchase-protocol identity by moving the `'cli:'` instance prefix into `common/src/constants/freebuff-desktop-sessions.ts` as `FREEBUFF_CLI_CLAIM_PREFIX`. The CLI package now imports this shared constant instead of maintaining a local duplicate in `cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-identity.ts`. This ensures the server and client use the same prefix to distinguish CLI execution claims from Desktop tabs under the versioned opt-in single-use protocol. Three file changes support this release, covering the constant definition, its CLI consumer, and the packaging manifest bump.

The constant `FREEBUFF_CLI_CLAIM_PREFIX` (value `'cli:'`) and the helper `isFreebuffCliClaim` are added to `common/src/constants/freebuff-desktop-sessions.ts` in the same commit, and `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` bumps the version from 0.0.203 to 0.0.204.

changes.what: Defines `FREEBUFF_CLI_CLAIM_PREFIX` and `isFreebuffCliClaim` in the desktop sessions constants file to provide a shared identifier for CLI purchase claims.
Replaces the local `CLI_MULTI_SESSION_PREFIX` with an import of the shared `FREEBUFF_CLI_CLAIM_PREFIX` to align CLI instance generation with the central constant.

eli5.text: Freebuff version 0.0.204 prevents your paid session from expiring when the app is closed by an outside force instead of you quitting normally. If your terminal window closes, the computer shuts down, or the app is otherwise interrupted by the system, your active time is now saved so you can pick up right where you left off on your next launch without paying again. The app also no longer abruptly shuts down and loses your work if the internal display engine freezes or encounters a severe glitch. When the tool does crash, it now saves a small report locally and automatically sends it to the developers the next time you open it, replacing the old method that required users to take screenshots of errors. Finally, a specific signal that could accidentally terminate the app when background processes were disconnected has been explicitly ignored, keeping the interface stable.

ai.title: Add /model command and inline chat admission for Freebuff sessions
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI now supports changing the AI model and session state from within an active chat. A new /model slash command opens an inline model picker, and a new chat admission flow holds queued messages and requests wallet consent when the user submits a prompt that requires a new or different session. Several other related changes accompany this feature in the same commit. These include a redesign of the help banner into a scrollable three-column layout, the addition of a ? shortcut to open help and a Left arrow shortcut to open chat history when the input is empty, and the removal of the /reasoning command.
ai.evidence: New files cli/src/state/freebuff-chat-store.ts (defining useFreebuffChatStore, openFreebuffModelPicker, and requestFreebuffChatAdmission) and cli/src/components/freebuff-chat-controls.tsx (rendering the in-chat model selector and consent prompt) are introduced, while cli/src/commands/reasoning.ts is deleted and cli/src/commands/command-registry.ts replaces the /reasoning command with a new /model command that calls openFreebuffModelPicker().
ai.unknowns: The diff does not state why the /reasoning command was removed instead of being integrated into /model. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

changes.what: Adds a /model command to open the model picker and removes the /reasoning command and its aliases.
Introduces inline chat admission and model switching controls that hold the message queue and prompt for spending consent.
Redesigns the help banner into a responsive multi-column layout and adds ? and Left arrow keyboard shortcuts for help and history.
Adds a persistent Freebuff-specific header and footer showing model, reasoning effort, and chat name above and below the main chat area.
Extracts the Freebuff ASCII wordmark into a dedicated utility module to be used by the login screen and chat header.

eli5.text: Freebuff users can now type /model in the middle of a chat to choose a different AI model or set how deeply it thinks, and a bottom status bar shows the current model and how to change it. When you type a new prompt while the assistant is waiting for a session to start, your message stays saved in the input box and the app asks for your approval to spend credits before sending it. This also means the old /reasoning command no longer exists, the ? key opens a new three-column shortcut guide, and the Left arrow key opens your chat history when the input box is empty. The button on the earnings screen for metered accounts now says Learn More instead of Open Earn.
